definition: Semantics is the aspect of language concerned with word meaning and how meanings are organized and used, including which word combinations are acceptable in a language. In this context, it refers especially to lexical meaning and how differences between languages can affect learning those meanings.

reasons: The definition goes beyond the packet by presenting a broad, general-purpose account of semantics (“the aspect of language concerned with word meaning and how meanings are organized and used”) that is not stated in the source text.

The packet supports lexical semantics and collocational acceptability in L2 learning, but it does not directly support the fuller claim about how meanings are organized and used across language in general.

The packet discusses “L2 lexical semantics” and learners’ difficulty acquiring word meaning (especially in verb–noun collocations), but it does not explicitly define semantics as “the aspect of language concerned with word meaning” or describe semantics in general terms beyond the study’s focus on lexical meaning.

Claims about semantics “how meanings are organized” and “including which word combinations are acceptable in a language” are only indirectly supported via an acceptability judgment task on collocations; the packet does not establish these as general properties of semantics.
